items.abstract_or_text: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by abnormal cortical activity, which can be captured using electroencephalography (EEG). Although machine learning (ML) has shown promise for diagnosing several neurological conditions, comprehensive evaluation of classical ML and deep learning (DL) methods, together with physiologically meaningful explanations, remains limited for RTT. This study analyses resting-state, eyes-closed EEG recordings from RTT patients and healthy controls using both power spectral density (PSD)-based ML and end-to-end DL frameworks. Classical ML models, including Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were trained on PSD features, while EEG-specific DL architectures, including ShallowConvNet, DeepConvNet, EEGNet, and EEG Conformer, were trained directly on preprocessed EEG signals. Subject-wise cross-validation was used to avoid data leakage, with balanced accuracy as the primary performance metric because it equally accounts for sensitivity and specificity. Random Forest achieved the best performance among the classical ML models, whereas EEGNet achieved the highest DL performance. An ablation study indicated that 4-second EEG epochs offered the optimal trade-off between model performance and robustness. Model interpretability was investigated using SHAP for Random Forest and occlusion sensitivity analysis for EEGNet. Both methods consistently identified delta and theta oscillations, along with centro-frontal brain regions, as key contributors to RTT classification. These findings show that both PSD-based machine learning and end-to-end deep learning methods can reliably identify RTT and highlight common neurophysiological biomarkers, offering an interpretable framework for EEG-based diagnosis and biomarker discovery for Rett Syndrome.

items.title: Major Revision, Minor Accountability: LLMs as Reviewers of Published Articles in Top-Tier Journals
items.abstract_or_text: With the growth of scientific output, the peer review system is approaching a breaking point: reviewers are increasingly hard to secure, and turnaround times lengthen accordingly. LLM-assisted or LLM-generated peer review has been proposed as a remedy, but how such models would treat manuscripts already published in top-tier journals, the closest thing the current system has to a gold standard of scientific validity, is not known. Here we assembled a corpus of 200 articles, each released under a CC BY 4.0 license and published in 2026, from 20 general-science, life-science, and clinical-medicine journals including Nature, Science, and Cell, and asked four current LLMs (two proprietary, two open-weight) to produce independent peer-review reports of each one under a blinded protocol. Their decisions were overwhelmingly harsh and starkly inconsistent with each other: 605 of 800 reviews (75.6%) recommended major revision or rejection, but the rate at which any single model did so ranged from 17.5% to 100% (p < 0.001), disagreement on manuscripts that had, by construction, already survived real editorial review at the journals in question. When the same manuscripts were doctored with one deliberately planted, field-specific methodological or statistical flaw, detection rates varied from 17.0% to 60.5% across models (p < 0.001). Recommending revision for papers that had already passed editorial review (low specificity) while missing flaws deliberately placed in front of them (low sensitivity), these models produce output that should be read for what it is: an uneven, framing- and model-dependent signal.

items.title: IndoNutriQA: An Indonesian Clinical Nutrition Question Answering Benchmark
items.abstract_or_text: Clinical Question Answering (QA) underpins Clinical Intelligent Decision Support Systems, but progress is severely limited for low-resource languages such as Indonesian by the absence of public domain-specific data. We introduce IndoNutriQA, an expert-curated Indonesian clinical QA benchmark of 911 question-answer pairs built from real clinical-nutrition reports. Rather than a large-scale training corpus, it is positioned as a high-quality evaluation resource: every pair is grounded in a clinically relevant context, enriched with structured metadata (anthropometric assessment, medical diagnosis, document provenance, chunk segmentation). Eight standardised question types following the Nutrition Care Process (NCP), including the Problem, Etiology, Sign and Symptom (PES) diagnosis statement, are answered for every report, which was written by a graduate-level dietetic intern, by one of three nutritionists. Answers are free-form clinical prose rather than extractive spans, and an expert validation study finds 6-10% of reference answers contestable. The dataset supports generative, extractive and retrieval-augmented QA as well as zero- and few-shot LLM evaluation. We report fine-tuned baselines (IndoBERT variants, mT5, RAG) with 5-fold cross-validation, learning curves and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and benchmark eight contemporary LLMs zero- and five-shot. We further calibrate our LLM-as-judge rubric against three expert raters (one RD, two nutritionists), finding it human-comparable on factuality and completeness but unreliable on clinical safety, and a human error analysis shows it misses unsupported content that the raters identify. IndoNutriQA is released to foster research in Indonesian clinical NLP and nutritional decision support.

items.title: Neuro-Metabolic and Vascular Dysregulation are Functional Biomarkers of Acquired Brain Injury
creators: Chong Chie, J. A. K. H.
items.abstract_or_text: Emerging clinical and neuropathological evidence suggests a direct link between traumatic brain injury (TBI) and neurodegenerative diseases (ND), but the mechanisms by which TBI contributes to ND onset and progression remain unclear. To bridge this gap, the NINDS TBI-ADRD consortium developed a diagnostic framework to guide the design and evaluation of TBI-ADRD experiments using translational neuroimaging (DCE-MRI, 18F-FDG-PET) and advanced image-processing pipelines. Neuro-metabolic and vascular dysregulation (MVD) and metabolic functional connectomics (MFC) were evaluated in 8-month C57BL/6J mice at 30- and 60-days post-injury (DPI). Both MVD and MFC revealed significant changes at 30- and 60-DPI that were sex- and injury side-dependent. Female mice showed greater regional MVD alterations, while MFC identified sex-dependent changes at 30-DPI that diminished by 60-DPI. These findings suggest that a single mid-life closed-head injury induces sexually dimorphic MVD and brain network remodeling, supporting the potential of MVD as a sensitive biomarker for improved clinical monitoring post-TBI.

items.title: Characterization of selective pressures acting on protein sites with Deep Learning
items.abstract_or_text: It is often useful, in the field of molecular evolution, to identify the selective pressures acting on a particular site of a protein to better understand its function. This is typically done with likelihood-based approaches applied to codon sequences in a phylogenetic context. However, these approaches are computationally costly. Here we adapt a linear transformer neural network architecture, which has been shown to be able to reconstruct accurate pairwise distances from sequence alignments, to identify selective pressures acting on individual amino acid sites, in the mutation-selection framework. We design different versions of the architecture and train and test them on simulations. We compare the results of one of our models to state-of-the-art likelihood-based methods and find that it outperforms them when it is applied to data that resemble its training data. Its performance decreases however when it is applied to datasets simulated with different parameter values. In all cases, our approach operates at a fraction of the computational cost of likelihood-based methods. These results suggest that such a neural network architecture can compare very favorably to state-of-the-art approaches to characterize selection pressures acting on coding sequences, but that it must be trained on datasets representative of empirical data.

items.title: Comparative evaluation of large language models for guideline-based oral cancer management: a standardized assessment of GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1, and Grok-3
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being investigated as tools for clinical information synthesis, patient education, and decision support. However, fluent language generation does not necessarily translate into clinically accurate or guideline-concordant recommendations. The extent to which contemporary LLMs can translate evidence-based oral cancer guidance into patient-accessible information and individualized clinical management remains insufficiently characterized. Methods We developed a standardized evaluation framework based on the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers, Version 2.2025. GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1, and Grok-3 were evaluated in two tasks: guideline summarization for non-medical audiences and case-based oral cancer management. Model outputs were assessed by three oral and maxillofacial surgeons across predefined dimensions, including accuracy, clarity, conciseness, logical coherence, diagnostic accuracy, treatment-regimen appropriateness, surgical planning, radiotherapy, systemic-status assessment, and prognosis. BLEU-4 and ROUGE-L were treated as exploratory text-similarity metrics. Results In the guideline-summary task, DeepSeek-R1 achieved the highest reported overall assessment score (8.8/10), followed by GPT-4o (8.3/10) and Grok-3 (7.8/10). DeepSeek-R1 also achieved the highest reported scores for accuracy (9.0), clarity (8.7), conciseness (8.7), and logic (9.2). In the case-based task, DeepSeek-R1 achieved the highest reported comprehensive score (87.44), followed by Grok-3 (77.77) and GPT-4o (68.61). DeepSeek-R1 achieved high reported scores for treatment-regimen accuracy (92), surgical-resection accuracy (93), radiotherapy-dose assessment (98), and prognosis (97). Grok-3 achieved the highest reported radiotherapy-dose score (100). The raw dataset also contains several anomalous values that require verification before inferential analysis, including a reported ROUGE-L value of 207 and several clinical scores of 20. Conclusions The three LLMs demonstrated distinct performance profiles rather than a uniformly superior model. DeepSeek-R1 showed the strongest descriptive overall performance in the current benchmark, particularly for structured treatment planning and prognostic assessment. However, clinically relevant variability was observed in staging, lymph-node management, surgical extent, HPV contextualization, and unsupported specificity. LLMs should therefore be considered assistive rather than autonomous clinical decision-support technologies. Larger multicentre studies using expert consensus standards and clinically meaningful endpoints are warranted.

items.title: Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents
items.abstract_or_text: Literature-searching language agents are becoming a standard component of scientific assistants for the life sciences, yet there is little controlled evidence on which parts of their harness matter. We run a controlled ablation on biomedical claim verification (SciFact) with the live PubMed API as the only tool. Holding the backbone and output format fixed, we compare four harnesses: closed-book answering, single-shot retrieval using the claim as the query, a ReAct-style agent that writes its own PubMed queries, and an oracle given the gold abstracts, each with two efficient frontier backbones. Naive single-shot retrieval finds the gold paper for only 6% of claims and turns overconfident errors into abstentions without improving accuracy. Letting the model formulate its own queries triples gold recall and yields the best verdicts (62% accuracy vs. 49-59% for the other realistic harnesses), although these differences are not significant at our sample size and agents use fewer than half of their search budget. With gold abstracts, the same models reach 79-86% accuracy, a significant 17-24 point gap showing that retrieval, not reasoning, is the main bottleneck. Finally, a citation audit shows that closed-book models cite PubMed IDs that almost always exist (327/335) but are almost never relevant: a cross-family LLM judge rates only 3 of 327 existing citations as relevant to the claim, versus 67% for citations produced by the search agent. Existence checks are therefore insufficient safeguards for scientific agents. We release code, prompts, and all cached tool calls at https://github.com/saqlain2204/real-pmids-wrong-papers.

items.title: Peripheral Biomarkers and Determinants of Survival for Patients with Melanoma Brain Metastasis Treated with Immune Checkpoint Blockade
items.abstract_or_text: BackgroundImmune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has become the standard of treatment for metastatic melanoma (MM). However, patients with melanoma brain metastases (MBM) are often excluded from clinical trials. Here we analyse patients within the real-world OxCITE cohort receiving ICB treatment for metastatic melanoma, with a focus on MBM, aiming to discern outcomes, prognostic factors and peripheral biomarkers. MethodsPatients eligible for ICB treatment were recruited prospectively. Demographic, clinical and radiological data were collected from electronic patient records. Plasma samples were collected prior to the first cycle of treatment for plasma proteomic analysis. Results307 patients were included, 81 of whom had MBM on commencing ICB. No difference in overall survival between patients with and without brain metastases was noted on multivariable analysis (HR=1.1, 95% CI 0.73-1.6, p=0.68), whereas hepatic metastases were associated with increased risk of death (HR 1.7, 95% CI 1.2-2.4, p=0.0019). Within the MBM group, steroid treatment (HR=2.5, 95% CI 1.3-5.0, p=0.006) was associated with poor OS, whilst treatment with single agent ICB (HR=1.9, 95% CI 0.86-3.9, p=0.11), symptomatic first presentation of MBM (HR=1.5, 95% CI 0.76-2.8, p=0.25) and anti-seizure drug treatment (HR=1.74, 95% CI 0.89-3.4, p=0.10) were not. Amongst all patients carriage of a BRAF mutation was associated with increased risk of MBM (OR 2.49, 95% CI 1.4-4.4, p=0.0007), and increased propensity to new brain metastases on ICB treatment (OR 2.5, 95% CI 1.1-5.9, p=0.036). Analysis of blood and plasma samples demonstrated that patients with MBM have altered haematological profiles, with raised NLR and increased plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein levels, reinforcing the distinct systemic features of MBM. ConclusionsIn this real-world cohort of patients receiving ICB for metastatic melanoma, the presence of MBM did not associate with worse OS. Conversely, baseline corticosteroid use was adversely prognostic. Intriguingly, plasma GFAP was significantly elevated in patients with MBM and correlated with the burden of intracranial disease, highlighting a potential role for GFAP as a candidate biomarker for MBM in high-risk surveillance. Our observations indicate the adversely prognostic weight historically attached to M1d disease is no longer applicable in the ICB era.

items.title: Source-linked multispecialty clinical reasoning and tumour-board decision-making in colorectal cancer
items.abstract_or_text: Clinical records preserve patient findings and final recommendations but rarely capture how specialists select evidence, develop alternative interpretations, disagree, and converge on a management strategy. We describe a dataset derived from ten retrospectively selected, completed cases of histologically confirmed colorectal cancer. For each case, an administrator uploaded de-identified textual clinical records to an authenticated web-based annotation platform. A medical oncologist, surgical oncologist, and radiation oncologist, each with more than ten years of clinical experience, independently linked relevant source fragments to patient-specific interpretations and documented clinical problems, differential hypotheses, uncertainty, and diagnostic and treatment strategies. After the three records were locked, a large language model generated candidate questions for review by the tumour-board chair. The four physicians then discussed each case online; recordings were automatically transcribed and verified by two medical residents. The dataset comprises 30 source-linked specialist reasoning records, 10 verified case-level discussion transcripts, 10 final tumour-board decisions, and associated provenance and quality-control metadata. It supports research on evidence-grounded reasoning, cross-specialty disagreement, multidisciplinary decision-making, and multi-agent clinical decision support.

items.title: Perisynaptic matrix gene variants underlie DystoniaGeneNet endophenotypes in isolated focal dystonia
items.abstract_or_text: Isolated focal dystonia is a rare movement disorder characterized by abnormalities in brain structure and function. The genes underlying isolated focal dystonia are not fully elucidated, and genetic studies are constrained by incomplete penetrance and small family sizes. Neuroimaging endophenotypes shared by patients and unaffected relatives can reveal genetic liability independently of clinical manifestation and offer a strategy for advancing gene discovery. We developed DystoniaGeneNet, a 3D convolutional neural network that predicts familial status from T1-weighted brain MRIs. We then used its predictions to guide genetic analyses in isolated focal dystonia. DystoniaGeneNet was trained on 40 patients with familial laryngeal dystonia and 40 healthy controls, then applied to independent cohorts of 21 patients with familial isolated focal dystonia, 364 patients with sporadic dystonia, and 98 unaffected relatives. Model predictions were incorporated into variant prioritization and segregation analysis in 214 individuals with whole-exome sequencing data, and results were replicated in another 738 independent exomes, in genetic data from a hospital-based biobank (892 dystonia cases, 2,475 controls), and in the All of Us Research Program genetic data (1,343 dystonia cases, 6,840 controls). DystoniaGeneNet discriminated familial dystonia from healthy controls in the training set and correctly classified 85.7% of independent familial cases, using a biomarker centred on the corpus callosum and inferior temporal gyrus. Across the discovery and replication cohorts, we identified rare, likely pathogenic genetic variants in RAP1GAP and TNN segregating with disease in families. Additional variants were found in singletons with isolated focal dystonia. In patients with clinically sporadic dystonia but predicted to have familial features, we observed multiple rare variants in ITSN2, including three high-confidence loss-of-function variants, and an enrichment of damaging missense variants in its Dbl homology domain. To determine the functional impact of discovered genetic variants, we assessed gene expression and splicing via qPCR and RNA sequencing (n = 74), revealing reduced RAP1GAP and ITSN2 expression in variant carriers. At the pathway level, rare nonsynonymous variants in brain-expressed matrisome genes were associated with dystonia (P = 0.012). Our strategy utilizing a deep learning-derived neuroimaging endophenotype to empower gene discovery uncovered RAP1GAP, TNN, and ITSN2 as novel genes associated with isolated focal dystonia. These genes converge on perisynaptic extracellular matrix-synapse signalling, implicating a mechanism linked to synaptic plasticity deficits, and identifying a molecular substrate for network-level brain abnormalities that characterize this disorder. Further, we exemplify a generalizable framework for leveraging endophenotypes in rare neurogenetic diseases with incomplete penetrance.

items.title: Convergent Performance, Divergent Mechanisms in LoRA-Adapted Vision Foundation Models for Brain MRI
items.abstract_or_text: Adapting Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) to medical imaging via LoRA has become standard practice, yet model selection is guided almost entirely by downstream task metrics, treating backbones with similar performance as interchangeable. We investigate whether equal performance implies equal internal representational shift. We analyse four ViT-B/16 backbones, DINOv3, SigLIP2, MerMED-FM, and BiomedCLIP, pre-trained with different objectives (self-distillation vs. contrastive vision-language) and on different data domains (natural vs. medical images). We adapt each to brain tumour segmentation and evaluate on six datasets covering both segmentation and Alzheimer's disease classification. Using attention divergence, weight-change analysis, and activation patching, we find that the four models converge to similar segmentation performance (mean Dice 78-81%) through markedly different internal dynamics, yet diverge in cross-task transfer: segmentation adaptation improves Alzheimer's disease classification for DINOv3 but degrades it for the other three backbones. We reveal a dissociation between modification magnitude and causal importance: the most heavily modified layers are not the causally relevant ones, with early-to-mid layers identified as sufficient for segmentation recovery. Restricting LoRA to these layers matches or approaches full-layer segmentation while reducing classification degradation in the three affected backbones, providing a mechanistically grounded strategy that is more parameter-efficient and more robust than standard full-layer adaptation.

items.title: Can Language Models Get "Aphasia" From Neuronal Ablation?
items.abstract_or_text: Progressive neuronal loss is the hallmark of neurodegenerative disease, yet how loss of neurons shapes the pattern of cognitive decline remains poorly understood. Here we systematically ablate neurons (computational units) in language models spanning recurrent long short-term memory (LSTM) and Transformer architectures and apply limited fine-tuning as a simple proxy for compensatory plasticity. With whole-unit ablation, LSTMs degrade gradually with syntactic and semantic faculties declining in parallel across mild-to-moderate damage. By contrast, Transformers exhibit late threshold-like collapse under feedforward multi-layer perceptron (MLP) ablation and smoother sigmoid-like decline under attention-head ablation. Qualitatively, MLP-ablated models continue to make within-category semantic substitutions (semantic paraphasias) alongside rising non-responses, paralleling Wernicke-type aphasia, while attention-head ablation produces a trend toward loss of semantic specificity similar to the semantic variant of primary progressive aphasia (svPPA). These findings indicate that feedforward and attentional pathways have functionally distinct failure modes, suggesting that architecture-dependent failure profiles may offer new computational perspectives on aphasic syndromes and neurodegenerative diseases as an in silico model. Notably, early accuracy retention under Transformer attention-head ablation qualitatively parallels pre-symptomatic reserve before the 40--60% neuronal loss reported by Gomez-Isla et al. (1996) when clinical symptoms emerge in Alzheimer's disease, whereas the steadier LSTM decline parallels the symptomatic progression described by DeKosky and Scheff (1990) and Terry et al. (1991).

items.title: ALSmiR: a curated evidence resource for ALS-associated microRNAs for biomarker discovery
items.abstract_or_text: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a multifactorial, late-onset neurodegenerative disease with incompletely understood pathogenesis. Limited survival after symptom onset creates an urgent need for biomarkers to support diagnosis, prognosis, and patient stratification. MicroRNAs are among the candidate biomarkers investigated in this disease. Although reviews have synthesized microRNA expression findings, differences in patient populations, biospecimens, and methods complicate comparisons. In the age of data-driven research, we need an updated, searchable resource that links each finding to its context and incorporates growing evidence. Here, we present ALSmiR, a public, manually curated database of polymerase chain reaction-based microRNA expression findings from human biological fluids and their components. ALSmiR currently contains 1,620 expression records from 49 publications comparing patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis with healthy controls, covering 816 microRNA names across 13 biospecimen categories. We link publication, cohort, and microRNA-result tables to preserve each finding's clinical and experimental context. We retain significant and non-significant results and provide searchable records and comma-separated values exports for independent analysis. We update ALSmiR annually and verify author submissions against source publications before inclusion. Researchers can use ALSmiR to assess candidate biomarkers, formulate hypotheses, and design independent validation studies. ALSmiR is freely accessible worldwide without registration at https://alsmir.dokhlab.org/.

items.title: QSGT: Quantum-Inspired Sparse Gated Transformer for Faithful Multi-modal Radiology Report Summarization
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Improving the alignment between visual evidence andtextual descriptions in medical vision-language models(VLM) remains a critical challenge for achieving entitylevelfaithfulness in low-resource generation tasks. Thispaper proposes Quantum-Inspired Sparse Gated Transformer(QSGT), a hybrid approach of token pruningand mixture of experts (MoE), grounded on the conceptionof quantum many-body wavefunction. This hybridapproach was aimed at improving the selectionof both modality-specific expert tokens and the formationof non-dominating experts to determine stableconjugates. The token pruning approach was improvedusing the quantum orbital style token assignments andthe mixture of experts by the quantum doubly occupancyapproximation. We also introduce two clinicallymotivated regularization terms, pair loss and seniorityloss, further enforce semantic consistency and dominanceof diagnostically relevant features. Our extensiveexperiments across seven thoracic disease categoriesdemonstrate that QSGT significantly outperforms stateof-the-art medical VLMs on multiple evaluation metrics,including RadGraph (36.2), SPICE (42.68), andconsistently high BERTScore (98), on the MIMIC-CXRtest set. QSGT achieves substantial gains in clinical correctnessand semantic accuracy, particularly for complexconditions such as pneumonia and pneumothorax. Ablationstudies confirmthe importance of each architecturalcomponent, while convergence analyses show stable andinterpretable learning dynamics. These results indicate that QSGT provides a robust and clinically meaningfulsolution for multimodal medical report summarization,enabling more reliable, interpretable, and patientcentredclinical AI systems.

items.title: From Structured Records to Patient Narratives: Preserving Clinical Alignment in LLM-Generated Health Summaries
items.abstract_or_text: As wearable and digital health systems increasingly generate longitudinal physiological records, communicating these observations in patient-accessible language remains a significant challenge. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising mechanism for translating structured clinical information into readable narratives, but this process may introduce semantic drift, where clinically precise meaning is distorted during simplification. We investigate evidence-grounded health summarization for menstrual health monitoring using a constrained generation framework that combines structured evidence conditioning with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) using a prompt-based constrained generation framework. We evaluate semantic alignment using Natural Language Inference (NLI), atomic factuality metrics, and readability measures. Across three LLMs and 4,500 generated summaries, explicit grounding constraints consistently improve clinical alignment, particularly by improving uncertainty preservation and, once faithfulness is evaluated against retrieved evidence, generally preserving or improving faithfulness, while effects on omission remain model-dependent. We also find that improved clinical alignment comes at the cost of increased reading difficulty and medical terminology. These findings highlight the need to jointly evaluate faithfulness, uncertainty preservation, and readability when developing patient-facing medical LLM systems.

items.title: Development of a deep learning model for glomerulus detection and segmentation in kidney histopathology images
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Estimation of nephron number, an indicator of renal reserve, requires quantitative assessment of glomerular number and size in kidney biopsy specimens. We aimed to develop an automated system for quantitative measurement of glomerular areas from clinical kidney biopsy images, across diverse kidney diseases. Methods: We developed a two-stage deep learning system combining Faster R-CNN for glomerular detection in whole-slide images (WSIs) and DeepLabV3+ for segmentation. Of 114 kidney biopsies (228 WSIs), 104 were used for model development and 10 for independent final evaluation. Agreement was assessed using the F1-score for detection, the Dice coefficient for segmentation, and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for glomerular area measurement. Analysis was performed at 40x total magnification (2.331 m/pixel) and validated against 400x images. Results: In the independent evaluation set, the artificial intelligence (AI) model achieved a mean F1-score of 0.851 for detection, compared with 0.888 among experts. For segmentation, the Dice coefficient was 0.959 {+/-} 0.011 and the per-pair ICC (2,1) for area measurement was 0.989 {+/-} 0.009; both were comparable to inter-expert agreement. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of -344 m2 (95% limits of agreement, -1904 to 1216 m2) between 40x and 400x measurements. Conclusion: The two-stage model achieved glomerular segmentation and area measurement comparable to expert agreement in independent clinical data, with detection performance approaching inter-expert agreement, and provided reliable measurements at low magnification. This automated approach may facilitate large-scale quantitative kidney pathology and nephron number estimation from clinical kidney biopsies.

items.title: SIM-UT: A User Simulation based Evaluation Framework for Medical Triage Chatbots
items.abstract_or_text: LLM-based chat agents are increasingly used for complex, multi-turn, multilingual medical triage in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet evaluation methods focus on single-turn, English-only benchmarks that primarily test the chatbots' knowledge. In practice, users are often confused, overwhelmed, or emotionally vulnerable, giving unclear, misspelled single-word answers or long messages in regional dialects, and the context of a conversation can shift rapidly. We propose SIM-UT (Simulation of User Behaviour for Triage), a multi-turn, simulation-based evaluation method that identifies ecologically valid, contextually relevant failure modes of LLM-based triage chat agents. Using SIM-UT, we evaluated three real-world WhatsApp-based health chatbots: a respiratory screening programme in India, a hearing health support programme in South Africa, and a diabetes and lifestyle coaching agent in Kenya. We compared a medically fine-tuned open model (MedGemma) against general-purpose frontier models (ChatGPT and Claude) across 5,000+ multilingual simulated conversation turns grounded in the personas, constraints, and communication patterns of the real user populations, over 2-4 iterative rounds. A key failure mode emerged in both model families: de-escalation risk. The agents initially identified medical emergencies correctly, but when the user minimised the symptoms without introducing new clinical information, they de-escalated, exhibiting clinically dangerous sycophancy, for example agreeing that vaginal bleeding in pregnancy was "not a problem" or that decreased fetal movements at 32 weeks "can be normal". We recommend user simulation-based behavioural evaluation, grounded in real user context and covering adversarial and edge cases, as standard practice for triage chatbots in production, so that safeguards can be added before deployment or in subsequent iterations.

items.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
items.abstract_or_text: Reinforcement learning (RL) is an effective way to strengthen the long-context reasoning of large language models (LLMs), but it needs training data that are long, diverse, challenging, and verifiable. Human annotation of such data is expensive, naturally occurring data are too scarce to sustain RL, and existing synthesis methods depend on external corpora or stronger teacher models, which become harder to obtain as the trained models get stronger. Recently, RL from zero data, in which a model learns from tasks it proposes itself, has achieved excellent performance, but existing methods target short-context tasks. Therefore, we propose LongZero, a method that lets an LLM improve its own long-context reasoning without any external data. Instead of writing questions and answers over existing documents, LongZero first has the model synthesize the question and answer with its supporting evidence in a compact structured form, and only then separately expands the evidence into a long multi-document context. LongZero combines these self-written multi-hop reasoning tasks with self-written multi-round retrieval tasks and trains the model with GRPO. We evaluate LongZero on two LLMs across five long-context reasoning benchmarks and compare it with RL on data synthesized from external corpora. Experimental results show that LongZero can generalize to real tasks, and outperforms both baselines, suggesting a viable and promising path to improving long-context reasoning of LLMs.

items.title: Block Diffusion for Longitudinal EHR: Accuracy, Efficiency, and Representation Trade-offs
items.abstract_or_text: Autoregressive (AR) models have proved effective for zero-shot prediction from longitudinal electronic health records, but impose strictly sequential generation on trajectories containing temporally clustered and interdependent clinical events. We investigate block-based masked diffusion (BD) as an alternative on MIMIC-IV under matched tokenisation, context length, model capacity, and evaluation conditions. Across block sizes, BD exhibits a clear quality--efficiency trade-off, with small-block configurations retaining much of the predictive performance of AR while enabling substantially faster inference. A representative B{=}8 configuration achieves approximately 1.43\times faster evaluation. Although generative rollout remains below AR in most settings, frozen linear probes on BD and AR representations achieve near-identical performance across clinical prediction tasks, indicating that BD learns comparably informative clinical representations. Increasing the denoising budget yields diminishing returns, while alternative decoding strategies provide limited gains. Overall, our results show that block diffusion is a viable and computationally attractive approach to longitudinal EHR modelling, with further improvements in iterative decoding offering a promising route toward closing the remaining generative performance gap.

items.title: Computer Vision and Knowledge-Grounded Language Models for Intelligent Beekeeper Assistance
items.abstract_or_text: Managed and wild bees sustain roughly a third of the global food products, yet colonies face mounting stress from climate-change including extreme weather patterns, altered parasite and disease patterns. Timely assessment of colony condition such as understanding colony strength, brood area, honey and pollen storage, comb usage, is essential to adaptive management. However, manual hive frame inspection is slow, costly, and quality depends on scarce expertise. We present an artificial targeted intelligent system framework focusing on edge deployable pipeline that turns hive frame photographs into interpretable and action-oriented inspection report. The pipeline includes an object detector to detect biologically-meaningful comb-cell classes; detections are distilled into structured fact schema; facts are converted into constrained factual text; the text triggers a grounded knowledge-base for interpretations and recommendations. Knowledge-base entries are required to be triggerable by evidence expressed in the fact schema. We built our system based on open source FAIRHiveFrames-1K dataset and favour reproducible, edge-deployable models over large general purpose frontier models. We additionally release FAIRHiveText-1K dataset that turns FAIRHiveFrames-1K dataset into interchangeable facts and text interpretation of the facts, making it easy for further LLM-based research into this area. We also propose a pathway to develop the grounded knowledge-base that will be helpful in providing interpretable and actionable reports from the facts.

items.title: Contextual Biomedical Language Models for Imbalance-Aware Drug-Food Interaction Classification
items.abstract_or_text: Drug-food interactions (DFIs) are essential to patient safety because they can alter drug effectiveness or cause side effects. Automated classification of DFIs is difficult because of unstructured textual data, semantic ambiguity, and class imbalance, especially when separating neutral interactions. This paper presents an imbalance-aware deep learning approach for classifying drug-food interactions into three classes: safe, neutral, and unsafe. A structured dataset is created from textual drug interaction descriptions by extracting drug-food pairs and labeling them using rule-based heuristics. To address class imbalance, we apply class weighting and focal loss while fine-tuning the context-aware BioBERT language model. Our experiments show that the approach reaches an accuracy of 85% and a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.77, with a notable improvement on the minority neutral class (F1-score of 0.56). The main novelty of this work is the combination of contextual biomedical language modeling with imbalance-aware deep learning, enabling more effective classification of DFI datasets.
